Menu
Help
Everything in TOOLSNEST works on your phone, offline. Tap a tool below to see what it does and how to use it, or read the common questions at the end.
How each tool works
Common questions
Show details
Hide details

Makes photos smaller in file size without visibly hurting quality.
1. Tap Select and choose one or more images.
2. Pick the output format and move the quality slider (lower quality means a smaller file).
3. Tap Compress Images, then Save or Share.
Tip: PNG is lossless, so the slider may not change its size much. Reducing the dimensions saves more space.

Changes the width and height of your images.
1. Choose one or more images.
2. Use Percentage mode, or type exact width and height (the aspect ratio can stay locked).
3. Tap Resize Images and save the result.
Tip: Extremely large output sizes are blocked to protect your phone memory.

Converts images between PNG, JPEG and WebP.
1. Choose one or more images.
2. Pick the Target Format and, for JPEG or WebP, the quality.
3. Tap Convert Images, then Save or Share.
Tip: JPEG has no transparency, so transparent areas get a solid background colour.

Cuts out only the part of a photo you want.
1. Pick a photo.
2. Drag the corners or edges of the box, or choose a fixed ratio such as 1:1, 4:3 or 16:9. Pinch to zoom the photo.
3. Choose JPEG, PNG or WebP and the quality, then tap Crop and Save.
The cropped picture opens on its own result screen with Save, Share and Open.

Removes hidden information from photos, such as GPS location, camera model and date.
1. Choose one or more images.
2. Review what hidden data was found.
3. Tap the clean and save button and check the verification result.
Tip: Use it before sharing photos online so your location stays private.

Shows the details of any file: name, size, type and other properties.
1. Tap Select and choose a file from your storage.
2. Read the File Properties list.
Nothing is changed or uploaded.

Creates a SHA-256 checksum, a unique fingerprint of a file, to prove it was not changed or damaged.
1. Select up to 20 files.
2. Tap Generate SHA-256 Hashes and copy the result.
3. To verify a download, paste the expected 64-character hash into the compare box. A match means the file is identical.

Packs many files, or a whole folder, into one ZIP archive.
1. Add files and/or a folder.
2. Type the archive name and choose the compression mode.
3. Tap Create ZIP Archive, then Save or Share.
Tip: Files that cannot be read are listed so you can continue without them.

Creates QR codes for text, website links, Wi-Fi, contacts, email and more.
1. Choose the QR type.
2. Fill in the details.
3. Tap generate, then Save or Share the image.
Tip: For printing choose a higher QR resolution in Settings (512, 1024 or 2048 px).

Combines several PDF files into one.
1. Select two or more PDF files.
2. Arrange them in the order you want.
3. Tap merge, then Save or Share the new PDF.

Splits a PDF into parts.
1. Select a PDF.
2. Choose a mode: Extract Pages, All Single Pages, or Custom Ranges such as 1-3, 4-7.
3. Tap split, then Save or Share the results.

Makes a PDF smaller.
1. Select a PDF.
2. Choose a mode: Optimize Images keeps text selectable, while Maximum Reduction turns pages into images (text can no longer be selected).
3. Tap compress and compare the new size.
Tip: A PDF that is mostly text may not shrink much.

Turns pages of a PDF into pictures.
1. Select a PDF.
2. Choose which pages to convert, and PNG (sharpest) or JPEG with a quality value.
3. Tap convert, then Save or Share the images.

Builds one PDF from several pictures.
1. Select the images in the order you want the pages.
2. Choose the quality (High or Medium) and page size (A4 or Letter; the default is set in Settings).
3. Tap create, then Save or Share the PDF.

Rotates pages of a PDF.
1. Select a PDF.
2. Pick pages: All, Odd, Even, or a custom range such as 1-3, 5, 8.
3. Tap a rotate button (90 clockwise, 180 or 90 counter-clockwise), then Save or Share the PDF.

Extracts the sound from a video.
1. Select a video.
2. Choose M4A (AAC) or WAV. If the video audio is already AAC it can be copied without losing quality.
3. Tap extract, then Save or Share the audio.
The default format and bitrate are in Settings.

Converts audio files to M4A (AAC) or WAV.
1. Select an audio file (MP3, WAV, AAC, M4A, FLAC, OGG or OPUS).
2. Choose the output format; for AAC pick a bitrate (higher is better quality and bigger).
3. Tap convert, then Save or Share.
Tip: Converting a compressed song to WAV does not improve its quality.

Makes a video smaller so it is easier to store and send.
1. Select a video.
2. Choose the resolution and quality, and decide whether to keep the audio. The estimated size is shown.
3. Tap compress. When it finishes, play the result in the preview and then Save, Share, Open or Save to Gallery.
Tip: Long videos take time. Keep notifications on so you can see progress in the background.

Cuts a part out of an audio file.
1. Select an audio file.
2. Drag the start and end handles on the waveform, or type exact times.
3. Choose the output format, tap trim, then Save or Share.

Removes the background of a photo on your phone, with no internet.
1. Select a PNG, JPEG or WebP image.
2. Wait for the cut-out result, then use the brush to restore or erase parts. Pinch to zoom for fine work.
3. Optionally pick a new background colour, then Save the result (PNG keeps transparency).
Tip: It works best when there is one clear subject.

Edit a PDF on your phone.
1. Open a PDF. Each page is shown sharply and cleaned up automatically if it is faded or blurry (the sparkle button turns this on or off).
2. Text: tap any text to change it. The old text is hidden with the page colour and the new text is written in a matching font and colour. Tap an empty spot to add new text. Use the size and colour options in the box.
3. Pen and Highlighter draw on the page. Signature and Image place a signature or picture.
4. Cover: drag over an area to hide it, optionally typing replacement text. Redact: drag over an area to black it out for good (that page becomes an image).
5. Pages: rotate, delete or add pages. Undo and Redo are at the top. Tap Save PDF when finished.
Tip: Pinch to zoom for precise edits. Scanned pages are re-saved sharper only when they needed cleaning.

Looks for signs that an image was made or edited by AI.
1. Select one or more images.
2. The tool checks hidden metadata, content credentials (C2PA), software traces and an error level analysis (ELA) heat map.
3. Read the verdict and the evidence list.
Important: the result is a hint, not proof. Missing markers do not guarantee a photo is real, and found markers do not always mean it is fake.
Do my files leave my phone?
No. All tools work offline on your device. The app does not upload your files anywhere.
Where do my results go after processing?
A result stays in a temporary place until you tap Save and choose a location, or Share it. Photos and videos can also go straight to the Gallery. Finished jobs are listed in the History tab.
How do I change the app language?
Open Settings and choose a language. The whole app, including this Help page, switches immediately.
What are the file size limits?

Limits protect your phone from running out of memory. Typical limits are about 50 MB per image, 150 MB per PDF, 500 MB per audio file and 1000 MB per video. If a file is too big the tool tells you before it starts.
A job is slow or seems stuck. What should I do?

Big files take time, especially videos. Keep Background Notifications on in Settings so progress is shown while you use other apps. If it still fails, try a smaller file or free some storage and try again.
How do I free up storage used by the app?
Open Settings. Turn on Delete Cache After Saving so temporary job files are removed right after you save. The Media Job Cache line shows how much temporary space is used.
Why is a video or PDF result almost the same size?
Some files are already well compressed, so there is little left to remove. Try a lower quality or resolution setting. For PDFs that are mostly text, the size cannot shrink much.
Why does the PDF editor not show some text as editable?

The editor finds text from the PDF itself, or from the picture of the page for scans. Very small, curved or decorative text may not be detected. In that case use Cover and drag over the area, then type the new text.
Which open-source software does the app use?

TOOLSNEST includes open-source software under its own licenses: Android Jetpack, Kotlin Coroutines, AndroidX Media3, PDFBox-Android and ZXing (Apache 2.0), ONNX Runtime (MIT) and the U2-Net model (Apache 2.0).
